top.title: Dubai Metro station to home in a driverless pod? RTA studies new transport routes
top.teaser: Dubai is studying plans to connect Metro stations with residential neighbourhoods, business districts and tourist attractions using driverless electric pods. The proposed routes are part of the Roads and Transport Authority's (RTA) Dubai Glydways project, which aims to make it easier for commuters to reach their final destinations through direct, on-demand transport. top.headline: RTA explores driverless pods connecting metro stations to communities
top.summary: The RTA is researching electric driverless pod routes to link metro stations with residential and business areas. This initiative aims to improve overall commuter accessibility across Dubai.
top.why: Better public transit connectivity directly influences residential area desirability and property values.

top.title: Dubai introduces digital Nol QR tickets for metro, buses and trams
top.teaser: Public transport passengers in Dubai can now use digital QR codes on their phones to access the metro, trams and buses, eliminating the need for a single-use red paper Nol ticket. Passengers can buy digital Nol QR tickets through the Nol Pay or S'hail apps, the Roads and Transport Authority announced. top.headline: Dubai launches digital Nol QR tickets for public transport
top.summary: Commuters can now access the metro, trams, and buses using smartphone QR codes via dedicated transport apps. This digital shift replaces traditional single-use paper tickets.
top.why: Improved transit convenience boosts the appeal of locations near public transport networks.

top.title: UAE turns to AI to fight fires: Find out how it will save residents, firefighters and protect properties

At the heart of the push is agentic AI, a form of AI that can act with a degree of independence. top.headline: UAE adopts artificial intelligence to improve firefighting and property safety
top.summary: The country is implementing agentic AI systems to enhance disaster response times and protect physical assets. Officials believe this technology will secure both residents and buildings more effectively.
